channel.title: The Practical Historian
channel.description: A spoken handbook of historical method: sources and evidence, argument and prose, historiography, forms of output, and research workflow.
channel.itunes:author: Study
channel.itunes:summary: A spoken handbook of historical method: sources and evidence, argument and prose, historiography, forms of output, and research workflow.

item.title: The Practical Historian 1: The Epistemological Foundation
item.description: Source versus evidence, witting and unwitting testimony, independence, the argument from silence, and what proof means in history.

item.title: The Practical Historian 2: Primary Source Analysis by Type
item.description: Reading the diplomatic, official, press, memoir, diary and visual genres against the grain.

item.title: The Practical Historian 3: Quantitative Methods and Their Limits
item.description: What data is as a source, and what quantitative instincts must be unlearned in the archive.

item.title: The Practical Historian 4: Essay and Argument Construction
item.description: Thesis, warrant, the paragraph as a move, counterevidence, and the uses of quotation.

item.title: The Practical Historian 5: Writing, Style, and the Form of Historical Prose
item.description: Prose choices as analytical choices: agency, modality, and the inherited vocabulary.

item.title: The Practical Historian 6: Working with Historiography
item.description: Reading secondary work as argument, mapping a debate, and positioning a contribution.

item.title: The Practical Historian 7: Forms of Output: Genre, Constraint, and Assessment
item.description: What each kind of deliverable is for, what makes it good, and how it is judged, including the abstract.

item.title: The Practical Historian 8: Research Workflow, with the Coda
item.description: The system that performs all of the above at scale: notes, tools, backup, and the use of IT and AI.
